messages:
sam: FYI getting a couple of support tickets about elevated p95/p99 since we rolled runtime v12 to the canary cohort ~30m ago. grabbing traces now.
deploy-bot: rollout started: runtime:v12 -> canary (10% traffic) at 2026-03-17T14:02:23Z :rocket:
mia: seeing p95 jump from ~120ms -> 420ms on text-gen endpoints for the canary tenant slice. p99 up to ~1.2s. grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/ABCD1234 (canary cohort) :grimacing:
leo: is this just the canary group or global? any 5xxs? auth errors? :thinking_face:
mia: only canary so far, no 5xx spikes, just tail latency. traces show a bunch of long kernel waits on a subset of GPU hosts.
support-nora: one customer (acme-inc) filed a complaint: "chat completions are taking 2-3x longer, impacting UX" — they included a timestamp and request ids. forwarding.
taylan: can we throttle canary traffic back to 0% and force traffic to v11 while we triage? prefer avoid full rollback if isolated.
infra-bot: canary cohort currently at 10% (hosts: gpu-canary-01..04). average p95 now 410ms (+290ms delta).
sam: good call. mia, can you run quick cohort split to 0% and start redirecting canary -> stable? if rollback needed it'll be faster.
mia: doing `redwood routes set-cohort --cohort canary --percent 0` now. also sampling traces for affected requests and collecting kernel selectors.
leo: hypothesis: kernel selector change in v12 picks a different attention kernel for seq_len ~512 which causes contention on NVLink on older hosts. can we force kernel selector to legacy for a test? also check batching params.
mia: test patch applied to one host (gpu-canary-02) forcing `KERNEL_STRATEGY=legacy`. p95 on that host dropped to ~130ms within a minute. putting results in the thread.
--- log snippet (gpu-canary-02) ---
```
[14:15:07] request_id=abc123 wait_kernel_ms=6 exec_kernel_ms=112 nvlink_wait_ms=2
[14:15:09] request_id=def456 wait_kernel_ms=820 exec_kernel_ms=95 nvlink_wait_ms=780
[14:15:10] request_id=ghi789 wait_kernel_ms=8 exec_kernel_ms=120 nvlink_wait_ms=3
```
(we see some requests with large nvlink_wait_ms only on hosts running v12)
sam: that's a pretty clear signal. plan: 1) set canary -> 0% immediately (mia done). 2) roll back runtime:v12 on canary hosts to v11. 3) open a bisect issue to narrow the change (kernel selector vs scheduler vs quant config).
taylan: rollback command: `redwood rollout undo --component runtime --version v12 --target canary --concurrency 2` — I'll run once canary traffic is 0.
mia: starting rollback on gpu-canary-01..04 now. will monitor p95/p99 and customer tickets. ETA ~6 minutes.
support-nora: ping me when rollback completes and I'll update acme-inc with status + ETA. they want a timeline.
leo: after rollback, let's create a small controlled perf test: same seq_len mix, two kernels (legacy/new) on identical host types to reproduce. also capture NVLink counters + kernel queue lengths.
infra-bot: rollback to v11 on canary hosts succeeded at 2026-03-17T15:11:23Z. canary traffic now at 0%.
mia: post-rollback p95 back to ~130ms, p99 under 300ms. closing immediate escalation. opening RFC and bisect ticket: BIS-2026-112 to track detailed bisect (kernel selector change in commit 7f9a3 -> candidate). assigning to @leo and @taylan.
sam: thanks team. good triage and quick mitigation. next steps: reproduce in lab, confirm root cause, and decide whether to re-ship v12 with a kernel selector fallback or adjust scheduling thresholds. keep support loop updated. :thumbsup:
